articles.title: How landscape gardening is being electrified
articles.summary: The switch to quieter electric equipment is not going as fast as some would like.
articles.content:
Part of the soundtrack to a day in southern California is the drone of petrol-powered gardening equipment.

Noise is one of the main reasons that cities around the US, external are banning petrol landscaping tools or encouraging electric alternatives.

These alternatives have the additional benefits of reducing carbon emissions, vibrations and the exposure of landscapers to pollution.

In addition they can mean longer working hours, as they can be used at times when residents demand quiet.

Today, I'm taking part in training run by the American Green Zone Alliance (AGZA), an organisation supporting the transition towards electric landscaping equipment.

To my surprise, the electric backpack leaf blower I strap on is not much heavier than my normal rucksack. Using the blower to herd balls around the park feels fairly intuitive, though naturally I'm much clumsier and slower than the pro landscapers.

As for noise, there's still a buzz, but the sound is higher-pitched and not quite so loud as the familiar petrol-powered machines.

The move to electric power is attracting new companies to the market for gardening kit.

US aerospace start-up Whisper Aero is one of those firms. Its main business is electric propulsion systems for aircraft.

But in 2022, after the Covid-19 pandemic made many people more sensitive to noise, and following a couple of years of research and development, the company realised that its aerospace-grade fans would work well in leaf blowers.

"Our technology is cleaner, quieter and more efficient than other air-moving technologies that exist today," according to Andrew Terajewicz, Whisper Aero's director of air management. "And the leaf blower is the perfect mix of this."

The battery on Whisper Aero's blower lasts up to 50 minutes at full power.

The company has had to scale up its manufacturing volume in its expansion to consumer technology.

Online pre-orders of Whisper Aero's handheld leaf blower started this year. It's priced at the high-end of electric leaf blowers, which are often more expensive than traditional petrol versions.

But for that you get a machine which is less likely to disturb the peace.

"It is so ultra quiet yet powerful, that the brain has a hard time understanding what's happening," says Dan Mabe, the former landscaper who founded AGZA.

Whisper Aero aims to further develop its products, including a backpack leaf blower that would be better suited to professional landscapers.
articles.reasoning: The article describes a meaningful shift from petrol-powered to electric landscaping equipment, which reduces noise pollution, carbon emissions, and health risks for landscapers. This transition has broad environmental and societal benefits, including quieter neighborhoods and cleaner air, supported by innovative technology from a company adapting aerospace tech to landscaping tools. The story provides sufficient detail about the technology, its impact, and ongoing developments, making it a substantive and inspiring example of environmental progress.
articles.personality_title: Electric leaf blowers are making gardening quieter and cleaner
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Many gardening tools in places like southern California use petrol engines that are noisy and polluting. Cities are starting to limit these tools to reduce noise and air pollution.

**What happened** – A group called the American Green Zone Alliance (AGZA) is helping landscapers switch to electric tools. A new company named Whisper Aero, which usually makes electric parts for airplanes, has created a quiet and powerful electric leaf blower. This blower runs on batteries for up to 50 minutes and is much quieter than petrol versions.

**Impact** – Electric tools like Whisper Aero’s leaf blower reduce noise pollution and harmful fumes. This means quieter neighborhoods, cleaner air, and healthier working conditions for landscapers. The quieter tools also let landscapers work longer without disturbing people.

**What's next step** – Whisper Aero plans to make more electric gardening tools, including a backpack blower aimed at professionals. The company is increasing production to meet demand and expects more people to choose electric tools over petrol ones.

**One-sentence takeaway** – New electric leaf blowers are helping make gardening quieter, cleaner, and better for workers and communities.

articles.title: Glass deposit operator confirmed after months of wrangling
articles.summary: Exchange for Change is running the new recycling programmes across the UK and will also run Wales's.
articles.content:
Officials had been in discussions with Exchange for Change for months, after it emerged there were key differences in what the Welsh government wanted from the operator and what it was prepared to deliver.

While the Welsh government was understood to require 3,500 reverse vending machines to handle glass at the outset of the DRS scheme, the proposal from Exchange for Change was to launch with 100 suitable machines around the country.

Those with knowledge of the discussions said this was a key sticking point.

Asked by BBC Wales if the Welsh government had changed its requirements for glass vending machines, Gruffydd said he "wasn't going to get into any particular figures" but that "we have to accept that we're on a journey here".

He added that the number of return points "would obviously increase" over time.

Wales is the only UK nation to include glass in its DRS and has faced a backlash from the drinks industry which warned of increased prices and reduced choice.

Referring to the concerns expressed by the drinks industry about increased costs and the complexity of having glass in Wales' DRS, Gruffydd said the government would be "working on exclusions for smaller producers and flexibilities around smaller retailers as well".
articles.reasoning: The article reports the confirmation of a glass deposit operator for Wales' new Deposit Return Scheme (DRS), marking a significant step in implementing a recycling program that includes glass—a first in the UK. This initiative has broad environmental benefits by promoting recycling and waste reduction on a national scale. The article provides context about negotiations and plans to increase return points over time, showing substance and meaningful progress in environmental policy.
articles.personality_title: Wales confirms glass recycling operator for new deposit return scheme
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Wales is starting a new recycling program called the Deposit Return Scheme (DRS). This program encourages people to return bottles and cans for recycling by giving them money back. Wales will be the first in the UK to include glass bottles in this system.

**What happened** – After months of talks, the Welsh government chose Exchange for Change to run the glass recycling part of the DRS. There were disagreements about how many machines would be needed to collect glass bottles. The government wanted 3,500 machines at first, but Exchange for Change planned to start with 100 and add more over time.

**Impact** – This decision is important because it sets up a new way to recycle glass on a large scale in Wales. Including glass in the DRS is a first in the UK and helps reduce waste and protect the environment. The plan to start with fewer machines but increase them later shows a careful approach to making the system work well.

**What's next step** – Exchange for Change will begin installing the glass return machines across Wales. The government will also work on rules to help smaller producers and shops take part in the program more easily. Over time, more machines and return points will be added to make recycling easier for everyone.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Wales has chosen a company to run its new glass recycling program, marking a key step in making glass recycling easier and more common across the country.
articles.personality_title_fr: Le Pays de Galles confirme l'opérateur pour le nouveau système de consigne du verre
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Le Pays de Galles lance un nouveau programme de recyclage appelé le système de consigne (Deposit Return Scheme, DRS). Ce programme incite les gens à rapporter bouteilles et canettes pour les recycler en leur rendant de l'argent. Le Pays de Galles sera le premier au Royaume-Uni à inclure le verre dans ce système.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Après plusieurs mois de discussions, le gouvernement gallois a choisi Exchange for Change pour gérer la partie recyclage du verre dans le DRS. Il y avait des désaccords sur le nombre de machines nécessaires pour collecter les bouteilles en verre. Le gouvernement voulait 3 500 machines au début, mais Exchange for Change prévoit de commencer avec 100 machines et d'en ajouter davantage au fil du temps.

**Impact** – Cette décision est importante car elle met en place une nouvelle méthode pour recycler le verre à grande échelle au Pays de Galles. Inclure le verre dans le DRS est une première au Royaume-Uni et aide à réduire les déchets et protéger l'environnement. L'idée de commencer avec moins de machines puis d'augmenter leur nombre montre une approche prudente pour que le système fonctionne bien.

**Prochaine étape** – Exchange for Change commencera à installer les machines de retour de verre à travers le Pays de Galles. Le gouvernement travaillera aussi sur des règles pour aider les petits producteurs et commerces à participer plus facilement au programme. Avec le temps, plus de machines et points de retour seront ajoutés pour faciliter le recyclage pour tous.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le Pays de Galles a choisi une entreprise pour gérer son nouveau programme de recyclage du verre, une étape clé pour rendre le recyclage du verre plus facile et répandu dans tout le pays.
articles.personality_title_es: Gales confirma operador para el nuevo sistema de devolución de envases de vidrio
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Gales está comenzando un nuevo programa de reciclaje llamado Sistema de Depósito y Devolución (Deposit Return Scheme, DRS). Este programa anima a las personas a devolver botellas y latas para reciclarlas y recibir dinero a cambio. Gales será el primero en el Reino Unido en incluir vidrio en este sistema.

**Qué pasó** – Después de meses de negociaciones, el gobierno galés eligió a Exchange for Change para manejar la parte de reciclaje de vidrio del DRS. Hubo desacuerdos sobre cuántas máquinas serían necesarias para recoger las botellas de vidrio. El gobierno quería 3,500 máquinas al principio, pero Exchange for Change planeó comenzar con 100 y agregar más con el tiempo.

**Impacto** – Esta decisión es importante porque establece una nueva forma de reciclar vidrio a gran escala en Gales. Incluir vidrio en el DRS es algo nuevo en el Reino Unido y ayuda a reducir la basura y proteger el medio ambiente. El plan de empezar con menos máquinas y aumentarlas después muestra un enfoque cuidadoso para que el sistema funcione bien.

**Próximo paso** – Exchange for Change comenzará a instalar las máquinas para devolver vidrio por todo Gales. El gobierno también trabajará en reglas para ayudar a los productores y tiendas más pequeñas a participar más fácilmente en el programa. articles.title: Giant whales move into Greenland waters as ice disappears
articles.summary: Melting sea ice from climate change has opened up the region for giant whales to undertake "feeding frenzies".
articles.content:
Sea ice has been disappearing from East Greenland, allowing giant whales to take advantage and move into previously inaccessible areas.

That is the conclusion of a decades-long study that has recorded - and filmed - hundreds of the world's biggest whales including humpbacks, minke and fin whales, feeding in ice-free seas along the coast in summer.

None of these marine mammals were historically found here as they have been locked out of the coastal waters by ice. Now, as climate change warms the sea and melts that ice, they have adapted.

Scientists describe the result as seasonal Arctic "feeding frenzies" - part of a major regime shift in the ocean environment along East Greenland.
articles.reasoning: The article reports a significant ecological shift where melting sea ice due to climate change has allowed giant whales to access new feeding grounds in East Greenland. This represents a meaningful environmental change with broad implications for marine ecosystems and biodiversity, highlighting adaptation and new ecological opportunities despite the underlying climate challenge.
articles.personality_title: Giant whales explore new feeding grounds in East Greenland as ice melts
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – For many years, thick sea ice covered the waters along East Greenland, making it hard for large whales to reach these coastal areas. The ice acted like a barrier, keeping giant whales such as humpbacks, minke, and fin whales away.

**What happened** – A long-term study has found that as climate change causes sea ice to melt during summer, these big whales are now moving into East Greenland’s coastal waters. Scientists have recorded and filmed hundreds of these whales feeding in areas that used to be blocked by ice.

**Impact** – This change shows how animals can adapt to new environments. The whales are having what scientists call "feeding frenzies" in the ice-free seas, which means they find plenty of food and eat a lot. This shift in whale behavior is part of a bigger change in the ocean’s ecosystem around East Greenland, affecting many sea creatures and plants.

**What’s next step** – Researchers will keep watching the whales and the ocean to understand how this new feeding pattern affects the whole environment. They want to see if the whales will stay in these areas year after year and how other parts of the ecosystem respond.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Melting sea ice in East Greenland has opened new feeding areas for giant whales, showing how climate change is changing marine life in surprising ways.
articles.personality_title_fr: De grandes baleines explorent de nouveaux sites d’alimentation au Groenland Est grâce à la fonte des glaces
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Pendant de nombreuses années, de la glace de mer épaisse recouvrait les eaux du Groenland Est, empêchant les grandes baleines d’atteindre ces zones côtières. La glace agissait comme une barrière, tenant éloignées les grandes baleines comme les baleines à bosse, les rorquals communs et les petits rorquals.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Une étude de longue durée a montré qu’avec le réchauffement climatique, la glace de mer fond en été, permettant à ces grandes baleines de se déplacer dans les eaux côtières du Groenland Est. Les scientifiques ont enregistré et filmé des centaines de ces baleines en train de se nourrir dans des zones auparavant bloquées par la glace.

**Impact** – Ce changement montre que les animaux peuvent s’adapter à de nouveaux environnements. Les baleines vivent ce que les scientifiques appellent des « frénésies alimentaires » dans ces mers sans glace, ce qui signifie qu’elles trouvent beaucoup de nourriture et mangent beaucoup. Ce comportement est un signe d’un changement plus large dans l’écosystème marin autour du Groenland Est, affectant de nombreuses espèces.

**Prochaine étape** – Les chercheurs vont continuer à observer les baleines et l’océan pour comprendre comment ce nouveau mode d’alimentation influence tout l’environnement. Ils veulent savoir si les baleines resteront chaque année dans ces zones et comment les autres espèces réagiront.

**Résumé en une phrase** – La fonte de la glace de mer au Groenland Est a ouvert de nouvelles zones d’alimentation pour les grandes baleines, montrant comment le changement climatique modifie la vie marine de façon inattendue.
articles.personality_title_es: Grandes ballenas exploran nuevas zonas de alimentación en el este de Groenlandia tras el deshielo
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Durante muchos años, el hielo marino grueso cubría las aguas del este de Groenlandia, impidiendo que las grandes ballenas llegaran a estas zonas costeras. El hielo actuaba como una barrera que mantenía alejadas a ballenas como las jorobadas, las rorcuales comunes y las rorcuales pequeños.

**Qué pasó** – Un estudio a largo plazo descubrió que, debido al cambio climático, el hielo marino se derrite en verano, lo que permite que estas grandes ballenas se desplacen a las aguas costeras del este de Groenlandia. Los científicos han grabado y filmado a cientos de estas ballenas alimentándose en áreas que antes estaban bloqueadas por el hielo.

**Impacto** – Este cambio muestra cómo los animales pueden adaptarse a nuevos entornos. Las ballenas están experimentando lo que los científicos llaman "frenesíes de alimentación" en los mares sin hielo, lo que significa que encuentran mucha comida y comen mucho. Este comportamiento es parte de un cambio más amplio en el ecosistema marino alrededor del este de Groenlandia, afectando a muchas especies.

**Próximos pasos** – Los investigadores seguirán observando a las ballenas y el océano para entender cómo este nuevo patrón de alimentación afecta al ecosistema completo. Quieren saber si las ballenas permanecerán en estas áreas cada año y cómo responderán otras partes del ecosistema.

**Resumen en una frase** – El deshielo en el este de Groenlandia ha abierto nuevas zonas de alimentación para grandes ballenas, mostrando cómo el cambio climático está cambiando la vida marina de formas sorprendentes.
